fact_check.claim: Student's NetID is the key information used to process mail; leaving it off can slow the box or return it
fact_check.note: Page says NetID is the key information; without it processing may be slower or the package returned to sender.

fact_check.claim: Central Campus center accepts packages of 50 pounds or less
fact_check.note: Stated for the Central Campus Service Center only. Headline and meta present 50 lb as a general Cornell limit; the article body correctly attributes it to Central.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's move-in advice: ship in as few boxes as possible, each under 50 lbs
fact_check.note: Page says 'as few boxes as possible, each under 50 lbs.'

fact_check.claim: Packages are held seven days after processing and returned to sender on the eighth day
fact_check.note: Matches. Stated on the Central Campus page.

fact_check.claim: Student gets an email when the package is processed; housing portal shows parcels under My Packages
fact_check.note: Email to NetID@cornell.edu and 'My Packages' in the Housing Portal.

fact_check.claim: Students should not pick up before the email/portal notice
fact_check.note: Page: students should not attempt pickup until they receive an email or portal message.

fact_check.claim: Mark food PERISHABLE in large, bold letters near the address; no refrigeration; processing can take a day or more; perishables must be picked up the day of notification or discarded; vendor packages usually processed same day
fact_check.note: All confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Service centers do not accept local deliveries such as DoorDash, Grubhub, Instacart, Walmart, Target
fact_check.note: Page lists exactly these services.

fact_check.claim: Amazon locker 'Dodgeball' outside Robert Purcell takes eligible Amazon orders under 35 lbs, 19 x 12 x 14 in, no perishables
fact_check.note: Matches (shipping weight under 35 lbs; product dimensions under 19 x 12 x 14 in; perishables not eligible; must be sold or fulfilled by Amazon).

fact_check.claim: Prohibited: small kitchen appliances (toaster, coffee pot, rice cooker, air fryer)
fact_check.note: Listed as prohibited.

fact_check.claim: Prohibited: candles, wax warmers, incense
fact_check.note: Candles, wax warmers, incense burners.

fact_check.claim: Extension cords and multiplug adapters prohibited; UL-approved outlet strip with breaker switch is the alternative
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Prohibited: peel-and-stick wallpaper, artificial plants, wall tapestries, curtains
fact_check.note: All listed.

fact_check.claim: Prohibited: halogen/'spider' lamps, bulbs over 150 watts; LED lights allowed
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Freestanding microwave prohibited outside Townhouse apartment kitchens
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Fans are fine, since air conditioners are banned and most buildings are not temperature-controlled
fact_check.note: Page confirms ACs are prohibited and fans are not prohibited (recommended). It does not say most buildings are not temperature-controlled; that clause is unsourced.

fact_check.claim: Cornell says not to ship medication with other items
fact_check.note: Page says 'Don't ship medication or other time-sensitive items.' The phrase 'with other items' in the table is a slight paraphrase; fine.

fact_check.claim: Medication goes to Cornell Health Pharmacy, ATTN Tracey DeNardo, 110 Ho Plaza, Ithaca, NY 14853; includes refrigerated prescriptions
fact_check.note: Matches exactly. Also on the student-service-centers page.

fact_check.claim: Service center types: North, Central, South Campus and West Campus house offices each have a shipping address, found on that unit's site
fact_check.note: Matches. The page also lists a Graduate & Professional Student Service Center (Hasbrouck), which the article omits.

fact_check.claim: Parcel Pickup Authorization Form in the Housing and Dining Portal lets someone else pick up parcels
fact_check.note: Matches (under Forms).

fact_check.claim: Packages sent too early may be returned to sender
fact_check.note: Page: packages sent well before the semester may be sent back.

fact_check.claim: Sorting takes longer at the start of the semester; 'wait until classes are underway'
fact_check.note: Source does not say sorting takes longer, and gives no 'wait until classes start' date. Unsourced hard claim attached to a cited link.

fact_check.claim: Carrier errors are returned to the carrier and redelivery may take up to two business days; packages sent to a previous campus address stay at that center; questions to scl-student-srv@cornell.edu
fact_check.note: All confirmed. The FAQ sentence has no inline link, though; add one.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Daily Sun, Jan 2023: first-years from warm places swapping hoodies for heavy jackets and snow boots; students looking forward to hot cocoa and blankets
fact_check.note: Article dated Jan 25, 2023 contains 'swapping hoodies for heavy jackets and snow boots' and a quoted student mentioning hot cocoa and blankets. Student-voice source used only for color, not a hard fact.

fact_check.claim: Student can use a microwave or kettle only where the building's kitchen provides one
fact_check.note: Source does not mention kettles or building kitchens. Kettle is not on the cited prohibited list, so the statement is unsupported.

fact_check.claim: 'It follows from ... what students in Ithaca say they do' (What to send intro)
fact_check.note: No source shows what Ithaca students say they send or do; the only student source is about warm-climate first-years' clothing. Implies evidence that is not cited.

beats_top.query: cornell care package ideas what to send student
beats_top.why: The #1 result is a generic 12-item parent blog post with no Cornell content, no shipping or dorm-rule guidance. Ours gives the Cornell mail process (NetID, hold period, perishables, prohibited items) with official sources, which is what a Cornell parent actually needs. It is weaker on concrete address and Ithaca-winter detail.
changes: Show a concrete example address format (name, NetID, service center street address) from an official Cornell page instead of only telling the parent to ask the student.
Make the 'what to send' section Ithaca-specific with a sourced fact or two (e.g. winter conditions from an official or news source) rather than generic packing ideas.
Remove or source the unsupported claims so every rule shown is traceable to the cited Cornell pages.

fixes: In 'Fans are fine', delete 'and most buildings are not temperature-controlled' (not in the source), or replace it with a sourced statement. Keep: air conditioners of any kind are prohibited and fans are not on the prohibited list; source https://scl.cornell.edu/sub/sub/residential-life/housing/housing-details/moving-campus/what-pack-what-not-bring

In the 'first box in August' bullet, delete 'and sorting takes longer at the start of the semester' and 'Wait until classes are underway'. Say only what the source says: packages sent well before the semester may be returned to the sender, so check the student's move-in dates with the service center before shipping.

In the 'Shelf-stable snacks and tea' bullet, delete 'The student can use a microwave or kettle only where the building's kitchen provides one' (unsourced). If kettles are mentioned, tell the parent to check Housing's prohibited list or ask the student, with a link to the what-to-pack page.

Replace the sentence 'It follows from the facts above and from what students in Ithaca say they do' with 'These are our suggestions, not Cornell rules' (no source shows what Ithaca students say they do).

Add the Central Campus example address from https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/service-centers-and-mail/central-campus-service-center: 'Your Name, NetID / 401 Willard Straight Hall / Cornell University / Ithaca, NY 14853', labelled as the Central Campus format only, and say other centers have their own addresses on their pages.
Add the Graduate & Professional Student Service Center (serves Hasbrouck) to the list of service centers in step 1, citing https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/student-service-centers.

Clarify in the title/meta/lead that the 50 lb limit is the Central Campus center's stated limit and Cornell's move-in guidance, and tell parents to check their student's own center's page for its limit.

In the FAQ answer on lost or delayed boxes, add an inline link to https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/service-centers-and-mail/best-practices-mail-and-packages for the two-business-day, previous-address and scl-student-srv@cornell.edu claims.

Make the winter advice Ithaca-specific: add one sourced fact about Ithaca winter conditions (official Cornell or National Weather Service climate page, with link) so the Winter basics bullet is not resting only on a 2023 student article about warm-climate first-years.
